metadata.title: Escape Room Countdown
metadata.theme: Completing all the challenges before time runs out
metadata.curiosityNote: Escape rooms make elapsed-time subtraction visible because every completed challenge uses part of the clock.

story.briefTemplate: Megan, Noel, Julianne, Rose, and Seraphina are determined to beat the most difficult escape room in their hometown. They are just advancing to the third and final challenge. They completed the Library in {quantity:library_minutes}, and the Labyrinth in {quantity:labyrinth_minutes}. If they have {quantity:total_escape_minutes} to complete the escape room, how many remaining minutes do they have to finish The Belltower?
story.causalEvent: The Library and Labyrinth used part of the one-hour escape-room clock.
story.closingNoteTemplate: The team has {quantity:remaining_minutes} to finish The Belltower.

label.child: Minutes used by the Library and Labyrinth

steps.prompt: How many minutes did they spend on the Library and the Labyrinth together?
steps.reasoningPrompt: The first two challenges both used time. What operation combines those minutes?

backwardCheck.prompt: Subtract the minutes used for the Library from the elapsed minutes. Do you get the minutes used for the Labyrinth?

steps.prompt: How many minutes remain for the Belltower?
steps.reasoningPrompt: The completed challenges used part of the hour. What operation finds the time left over?

backwardCheck.prompt: Add the elapsed minutes back to the remaining minutes. Do you return to the full hour?

operatorExperiments.alternateWorldTemplate: This matches the story: the Library minutes and Labyrinth minutes combine into the elapsed time.
Subtracting would fit a different question about the gap between the first two challenge times.
Multiplying would fit a different question about repeated challenge times.
Dividing would fit a different question about sharing the time into equal parts.
Adding would fit a story where the elapsed minutes were added onto the hour instead of taken from it.
This matches the story: the completed challenges use part of the hour, leaving time for The Belltower.
Multiplying would fit a different question about equal groups of minutes.
Dividing would fit a different question about sharing the hour into equal time blocks.

recap.headline: Why they have {quantity:remaining_minutes} for the Belltower
causalChain: The Labyrinth took {quantity:labyrinth_minutes}, so the first two challenges used {quantity:elapsed_minutes}.
The escape room allows {quantity:total_escape_minutes}, leaving {quantity:remaining_minutes} for The Belltower.

dataQuestion.prompt: What does {quantity:remaining_minutes} represent in the escape-room model?
dataQuestion.correctFeedback: Right. {quantity:remaining_minutes} is the time left for The Belltower.
dataQuestion.incorrectFeedback: That amount is the time left after the Library and the Labyrinth: {quantity:remaining_minutes}.
